page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-4-lssd is an ARM-based, memory-optimized server instance powered by the c4a family. It features 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 3.0 GHz, with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, it includes a bundled 402 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage, while lacking any GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate a balanced performance profile with notable strengths in memory operations. The instance achieves a strong Passmark memory score and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 32.26 GB/sec. However, raw compute benchmarks show limitations, with a weak Passmark CPU score and poor performance in CPU encryption tests. Memory bandwidth is measured at 494.32 GB/sec for cached reads and 102.77 GB/sec for uncached reads, while large-block write bandwidth is lower at 36.96 GB/sec.

Given its high memory density and bundled local NVMe storage, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring rapid data access without massive compute overhead. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis (achieving 8.56 million SET operations per second), and static web serving. It is less suitable for cryptographic tasks or LLM inference, where it exhibits weak to poor processing speeds.

It delivers 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and includes a bundled 402 GB NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage. Performance benchmarks show strong memory capabilities, highlighted by a top-tier Passmark memory score and 32.26 GB/sec single-threaded gzip compression.
